thread:
marta_pm: Quick sync — we need to finalize the 'entry lane scheduling' heuristics for the model catalog. Customer Acme wants: NA/EU/APAC staggered rollouts, ability to pin v1.2 but auto-fallback to v1.1 on regressions, and a clear SLA for pinned versions. Proposed: benchmark interop check + hardware-aware tagging + a 2-stage canary (shadow 10% -> canary 1% -> full). Thoughts?

sam_eng: +1 on hardware tags. We should gate by both latency p95 and token cost delta. If new model increases p95 by >15ms OR cost/token by >8% -> fail canary.

jia_sre: Re: SLA — pinned versions are customer-facing commitment. If we allow auto-fallback, need alerting and a rollback SLA (e.g., 15m for critical regressions). Also require a fallback model pinned in the customer config.

olga_prod: Agree on rollback SLA. Ops question: do we let customers opt into auto-swap or require explicit approval? For enterprise deals they want explicit approval + migration credits. For self-serve, opt-in by default with email notice?

ryan_se: Sales feedback: enterprise legal wants migration windows and a 30-day notice for major changes. For minor patch bumps (x.y.z) they expect faster cutover. We should encode "change_class" in the catalog metadata.

sam_eng: Proposed metadata fields: "change_class": [major, minor, patch], "hardware_affinity": [A100, H100, T4], "bench_profile_id": string. We'll use bench_profile_id to pick the right perf baseline per region/hw.

marta_pm: Nice. How do we handle benchmark interop across regions? We saw a model pass in NA but failed in APAC due to cold-starts on smaller GPUs.

sam_eng: Bench interop plan: run bench suites per bench_profile_id across representative infra: small (T4), med (A10/A100), large (H100). Require pass on at least 2/3 classes OR a documented mitigation (quantized variant or latency shim). If APAC fails but NA passes, we put APAC on "limited roll" and block full pin.

jia_sre: Add traffic routing policy: for limited roll, route <=2% traffic from that region to the new model. Monitor 1h rolling p95 and error rate. If stable -> bump to 20% then full. Need automation for bump/rollback.

olga_prod: For customer comms: standard template that explains bench results + region scoping + migration credits if they opt into manual cutover. Also attach a short explainer of what "pin" means (SLA + rollback plan).

ryan_se: Also add opt-out clause for customers with pinned contracts. If they decline automatic upgrades, we show them the "compatibility shim" support option (extra cost).

sam_eng: Quick config sketch (will add to RFC):
```yaml
model_entry:
  bench_profile_id: bench-v2-latency
  change_class: minor
  hardware_affinity: [A100,H100]
  rollout_strategy:
    - type: shadow
      pct: 10
      duration: 2h
    - type: canary
      pct: 1
      duration: 1h
    - type: ramp
      pct: 100
      duration: 24h
  gates:
    latency_p95_delta_ms: 15
    cost_pct_delta: 8
    error_rate_delta_pct: 0.5
```

marta_pm: Perfect. What's the cutover policy for pinned versions specifically? I want a clear step-by-step so support/sales can explain to customers.

jia_sre: Pinned cutover policy (draft):
1) Owner submits migration bundle with bench_profile + target versions + fallback.
2) System runs interop benches across required hardware/regions.
3) If pass -> shadow 10% for 2h (metrics collection).
4) If stable -> canary 1% for 1h.
5) If canary passes -> notify customer 24h window for manual opt-out. If no opt-out -> automated ramp.
6) If any gate fails -> auto-fallback to pinned fallback and page owner; initiate rollback SLA.

olga_prod: We should add a "grace credit" for customers who opt into early cutover (like 3 months free of migration risk) — helps incentivize adoption. Define eligibility: enterprise customers only or anyone above X monthly usage.

ryan_se: Sales likes the credit idea. Suggest: credits applied as % of monthly usage for first 30 days post-cutover if customer reports issues and we had to rollback.

sam_eng: Ops note: need automation for "fallback pins" and for creating canary cohorts by customer tenancy. Also need a UI in console to show bench results per region/hw and the time series used for gating.

marta_pm: Action items: @sam_eng create RFC with config sketch + bench matrix. @jia_sre write rollback SLA draft. @olga_prod draft comm templates and credit policy. @ryan_se compile legal asks for "change_class" and notice windows. I'll coordinate a 30-min review next Tue.

deploy-bot: New RFC created: rfc/entry-lane-scheduling-1715009999 (link: https://redwood.in/rfc/1715009999)

sam_eng: I added a short checklist to the RFC: bench-profile mapping, hardware matrix, gating thresholds, fallback config, console fields.

olga_prod: One more ask — include a "migration runbook" with exact owner on-call steps and rollback commands. Customers sometimes ask for a third-party runbook during audits.

jia_sre: Will include runbook skeleton. Also recommend a post-cutover 72h monitoring window where extra retention is enabled for traces/kv cache logs.

marta_pm: Thanks everyone. If there are no objections, I'll lock the RFC by EOD Fri and start drafting the internal playbook for support. :thumbsup:

sam_eng: No objections from eng. :rocket:

ryan_se: Sales aligned. Will flag legal items in the RFC comments.

olga_prod: Approved from product side.

jia_sre: Approved from SRE side.

marta_pm: Closing thread — see RFC link above for details.
